title: Débattre sur des dilemmes éthiques / Debating ethical dilemmas
bridge: In Spanish we use the subjunctive similarly to French, but there are key differences: in French, after expressions like 'il est important que' or 'je ne pense pas que', the subjunctive is obligatory, whereas in Spanish sometimes the indicative can be used depending on the context. Also, the French conditional is used for hypotheses similarly to Spanish, but in French the sequence of tenses in indirect speech is more rigid. Be careful with the use of 'pour que' and 'afin que', which are always followed by the subjunctive in French, just like 'para que' in Spanish, but with nuances of register.
rule: In French, to debate, structures that express opinion, hypothesis, and moral obligation are used. Impersonal expressions like 'il est essentiel que', 'il faut que', 'il est injuste que' require the subjunctive. Opinion verbs in negative or interrogative forms ('je ne pense pas que', 'penses-tu que') also govern the subjunctive. Hypothesis is expressed with 'si + imparfait (indicatif) + conditionnel présent' (si j'avais le choix, je prendrais...). To argue, connectors like 'd'un côté... de l'autre côté', 'en revanche', 'par conséquent' are used. In indirect speech, verb tenses undergo a transformation: if the main verb is in the past, the present becomes imperfect, the future becomes conditional, etc. Additionally, to express an unreal condition in the past, 'si + plus-que-parfait + conditionnel passé' is used. It is important to master the subjunctive in expressions of ethical evaluation (c'est bien que, c'est dommage que) and the negation with 'ne... que' which is not a negation but a restriction.

concept_examples.text: Il est crucial que nous respections la vie privée des autres.
concept_examples.translation: It is crucial that we respect others' privacy.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛ kʁysjɛl kə nu ʁɛspɛktjɔ̃ la vi pʁive de zotʁ/

concept_examples.text: Si l'on savait toutes les conséquences, on agirait autrement.
concept_examples.translation: If one knew all the consequences, one would act differently.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si lɔ̃ savɛ tut le kɔ̃sekɑ̃s, ɔ̃ aʒiʁɛ otʁəmɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: Je ne suis pas convaincu que la peine de mort soit juste.
concept_examples.translation: I am not convinced that the death penalty is just.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa kɔ̃vɛ̃ky kə la pɛn də mɔʁ swa ʒyst/

concept_examples.text: D'un côté, la liberté d'expression est fondamentale, mais d'un autre, elle peut nuire à autrui.
concept_examples.translation: On one hand, freedom of expression is fundamental, but on the other, it can harm others.
concept_examples.phonetic: /dɛ̃ kot, la libɛʁte dɛkspʁɛsjɔ̃ ɛ fɔ̃damɑ̃tal, mɛ dɛ̃ otʁ, ɛl pø nɥiʁ a otʁɥi/

common_error.wrong: Je ne pense pas que c'est une bonne idée de mentir.
common_error.correct: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée de mentir.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne pense pas que ce soit une bonne idée de mentir.
common_error.explanation: Many Spanish speakers use the indicative after 'ne pas penser que', but in French, when the main verb is negated, the subjunctive is required. In Spanish, one says 'no pienso que es' (although 'sea' is also accepted), but in French the rule is stricter: always subjunctive. To avoid this, remember that any expression of doubt or negation (ne pas penser, ne pas croire, ne pas être sûr) is followed by the subjunctive.

examples.original: À mon avis, la technologie pose des questions éthiques complexes.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ avi, la tɛknɔlɔʒi pɔz de kɛstjɔ̃ etik kɔ̃plɛks/
examples.translation: In my opinion, technology raises complex ethical questions.
examples.note: Use 'à mon avis' like 'in my opinion'. Note that 'poser des questions' translates as 'to raise questions'.

examples.original: Je trouve que l'euthanasie devrait être légalisée dans certains cas.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə løtənazi dəvʁɛ ɛtʁ leɡalize dɑ̃ sɛʁtɛ̃ ka/
examples.translation: I think euthanasia should be legalized in certain cases.
examples.note: The verb 'trouver que' is constructed with the indicative in affirmative, but with the subjunctive in negative.

examples.original: Pour ma part, je suis contre l'expérimentation animale.
examples.phonetic: /puʁ ma paʁ, ʒə sɥi kɔ̃tʁ lɛkspeʁimɑ̃tasjɔ̃ animal/
examples.translation: For my part, I am against animal experimentation.
examples.note: 'Être contre' requires the preposition 'contre' (without 'de' as in Spanish 'en contra de').

examples.original: Si j'étais à votre place, je refuserais de participer à ce projet.
examples.phonetic: /si ʒetɛ a vɔtʁ plas, ʒə ʁəfyzʁɛ də paʁtisip‿e a sə pʁɔʒɛ/
examples.translation: If I were in your place, I would refuse to participate in this project.
examples.note: Present hypothetical structure: si + imparfait + conditionnel. In Spanish, the imperfect subjunctive is also used.

examples.original: Au cas où il y aurait un conflit d'intérêts, je devrais me récuser.
examples.phonetic: /o ka u il i oʁɛ ɛ̃ kɔ̃fli dɛ̃teʁɛ, ʒə dəvʁɛ mə ʁekyze/
examples.translation: In case there were a conflict of interest, I would have to recuse myself.
examples.note: The expression 'au cas où' is always followed by the conditional. In Spanish, the subjunctive is used.

examples.original: Si l'on avait su les risques, on aurait agi différemment.
examples.phonetic: /si lɔ̃ avɛ sy le ʁisk, ɔ̃ oʁɛ aʒi difeʁamɑ̃/
examples.translation: If we had known the risks, we would have acted differently.
examples.note: Past hypothesis: si + plus-que-parfait + conditionnel passé. It is similar to Spanish: si + pluperfect subjunctive + compound conditional.

examples.original: Il est vrai que la transparence est importante, cependant elle ne doit pas compromettre la sécurité.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ vʁɛ kə la tʁɑ̃spaʁɑ̃s ɛt‿ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃t, səpɑ̃dɑ̃ ɛl nə dwa pa kɔ̃pʁɔmɛtʁ la sekyʁite/
examples.translation: It is true that transparency is important, however, it must not compromise security.
examples.note: The connector 'cependant' is equivalent to 'however'. In the expression 'il est vrai que', the indicative is used.

examples.original: Je comprends votre point de vue, mais en revanche, je considère que les animaux ont des droits.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə kɔ̃pʁɑ̃ vɔtʁ pwɛ̃ də vy, mɛ ɑ̃ ʁəvɑ̃ʃ, ʒə kɔ̃sideʁ kə lez‿animo ɔ̃ de dʁwa/
examples.translation: I understand your point of view, but on the other hand, I consider that animals have rights.
examples.note: 'En revanche' introduces an objection. Do not confuse with 'en cambio' (which can also be 'par contre', but 'par contre' is more colloquial).

examples.original: Bien que l'argent ne fasse pas le bonheur, il contribue à une vie plus confortable.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə laʁʒɑ̃ nə fɑs pa lə bɔnœʁ, il kɔ̃tʁiby a yn vi ply kɔ̃fɔʁtabl/
examples.translation: Although money does not bring happiness, it contributes to a more comfortable life.
examples.note: The conjunction 'bien que' requires the subjunctive. In Spanish, 'aunque' is used with subjunctive or indicative depending on the nuance.

examples.original: Il ne faut pas confondre éthique et morale, car l'une est universelle alors que l'autre est culturelle.
examples.phonetic: /il nə fo pa kɔ̃fɔ̃dʁ etik e mɔʁal, kaʁ lyn ɛt‿ynivɛʁsɛl alɔʁ kə lotʁ ɛ kyltyʁɛl/
examples.translation: One must not confuse ethics and morality, because one is universal while the other is cultural.
examples.note: The use of 'alors que' introduces a contrast (while). In French, the subjunctive is not used here.

title: Négocier et conclure un accord / Negotiating and closing a deal
bridge: In Spanish, to express conditions and agreements we use the subjunctive with relative freedom (Si tuviera tiempo, iría). In French, tense agreement in hypotheses follows strict rules: after 'si' the conditional is never used, but the imperfect is (Si j'avais le temps, j'irais). Furthermore, professional French relies on fixed formulas such as 'je vous propose' or 'on est d'accord' that differ from Spanish in their construction. This is a key point to avoid frequent errors in meetings.
rule: In French, to express conditions and negotiations, the structure 'si + imparfait, conditionnel présent' is used for hypotheses in the present/future. Example: Si nous baissions le prix, ils signeraient le contrat. The conditional is never used after 'si' (typical error: *Si nous baisserions...). For proposals and agreements, modal expressions such as 'je propose que + subjonctif' (Je propose que nous fixions une réunion) or the conditional of politeness (Je voudrais/J'aimerais) are used. The subjunctive is obligatory after 'pour que', 'bien que' and certain conjunctions. In negotiation, verbs like 'négocier, conclure, proposer, accepter, refuser, marchander' dominate, and connectors such as 'en revanche', 'par contre', 'd'une part... d'autre part' are used. Also common is the use of the pronoun 'on' instead of 'nous' in oral register.

concept_examples.text: Si nous réduisons le prix, nous pourrons conclure l'accord.
concept_examples.translation: If we reduce the price, we will be able to close the deal.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si nu ʁedyzɔ̃ lə pʁi, nu puʁɔ̃ kɔ̃klyʁ lakɔʁ/

concept_examples.text: Je propose que nous fixions une prochaine réunion.
concept_examples.translation: I propose that we set a next meeting.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pʁɔpoz kə nu fiksjɔ̃ yn pʁɔʃɛn ʁe ynjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: J'aimerais discuter des modalités de paiement.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to discuss the payment terms.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒɛmʁɛ diskjte de mɔdalite də pɛmɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: En revanche, nous ne pouvons pas accepter ces conditions.
concept_examples.translation: On the other hand, we cannot accept these conditions.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ ʁəvɑ̃ʃ, nu nə puvɔ̃ pa aksɛpte se kɔ̃disjɔ̃/

common_error.wrong: Si nous baisserions le prix, ils accepteraient.
common_error.correct: Si nous baissions le prix, ils accepteraient.
common_error.correct_alt: Si nous baissons le prix, ils accepteront.
common_error.explanation: The error comes from directly transferring the Spanish 'si bajaríamos' to French. In French, after a conditional 'si', the imperfect is used (not the conditional). It is a fixed rule: never use the conditional after 'si' in a hypothesis. To avoid it, remember that the structure is 'si + imparfait, conditionnel présent' when the condition is hypothetical, or 'si + présent, futur simple' if it is likely. Practice with pairs like 'Si j'avais (not: aurais) le temps, je viendrais.'

examples.original: Si nous augmentons la commande, obtenez-vous une remise ?
examples.phonetic: /si nu oɡmɑ̃tɔ̃ la kɔ̃mɑ̃d, ɔbtəne vu yn ʁəmiz ?/
examples.translation: If we increase the order, do you get a discount?
examples.note: Conditional structure with 'si + présent' in a formal question. Use the polite pronoun 'vous'.

examples.original: À condition que vous livriez avant vendredi, nous signerons.
examples.phonetic: /a kɔ̃disjɔ̃ kə vu livʁje avɑ̃ vɑ̃dʁədi, nu siɲʁɔ̃./
examples.translation: Provided that you deliver before Friday, we will sign.
examples.note: The phrase 'à condition que' requires the subjunctive (livriez). It is a typical pattern in negotiations.

examples.original: Je n'accepterai que si vous réduisez le délai.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə naksɛptəʁe kə si vu ʁedɥize lə delɛ./
examples.translation: I will only accept if you reduce the deadline.
examples.note: The structure 'ne... que si' adds emphasis. Note the use of the future after 'si' in a real condition.

levels.label: Faire des propositions et des contre-offres

examples.original: Je vous propose un compromis : une réduction de 10 % en échange d'un contrat de trois ans.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu pʁɔpoz œ̃ kɔ̃pʁɔmi : yn ʁedyksjɔ̃ də dis puʁɑ̃tɑ̃ ɑ̃ eʃɑʒ dœ̃ kɔ̃tʁa də tʁwɑ zɑ̃./
examples.translation: I propose a compromise to you: a 10% reduction in exchange for a three-year contract.
examples.note: The verb 'proposer' is used with an indirect object (vous). To express exchange, 'en échange de' is used.

examples.original: En contrepartie, nous pourrions envisager un partenariat.
examples.phonetic: /ɑ̃ kɔ̃tʁəpaʁti, nu puʁjɔ̃ ɑ̃vizaʒe œ̃ paʁtənaʁja./
examples.translation: In return, we could consider a partnership.
examples.note: 'En contrepartie' is equivalent to 'in return'. The conditional 'pourrions' softens the proposal.

examples.original: Seriez-vous prêt à baisser vos tarifs si nous nous engageons sur une plus grande quantité ?
examples.phonetic: /səʁje vu pʁɛ a bɛse vo taʁif si nu nu ɑ̃ɡaʒɔ̃ syʁ yn ply ɡʁɑ̃d kɑ̃tite ?/
examples.translation: Would you be willing to lower your rates if we commit to a larger quantity?
examples.note: The polite conditional 'seriez-vous' is typical in negotiations. The conditional structure in the question uses 'si + présent'.

examples.original: Je pense que nous avons trouvé un terrain d'entente.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə nu avɔ̃ tʁuve œ̃ tɛʁɛ̃ dɑ̃tɑ̃t./
examples.translation: I think we have found common ground.
examples.note: The expression 'terrain d'entente' is idiomatic and means 'common ground'. It is used to indicate progress.

examples.original: Dans ce cas, nous pouvons conclure le marché.
examples.phonetic: /dɑ̃ sə ka, nu puvɔ̃ kɔ̃klyʁ lə maʁʃe./
examples.translation: In that case, we can close the deal.
examples.note: 'Conclure le marché' is equivalent to 'close the deal'. The verb 'conclure' is irregular, but in the present it is 'concluons' (nous).

examples.original: Nous allons rédiger le contrat et vous l'envoyer pour signature.
examples.phonetic: /nu zalɔ̃ ʁediʒe lə kɔ̃tʁa e vu lɑ̃vwaje puʁ siɲatyʁ./
examples.translation: We are going to draft the contract and send it to you for signature.
examples.note: The structure 'aller + infinitif' expresses the near future. 'Vous l'envoyer' is the order of double pronouns: COD (l') + COI (vous).

title: Parler de littérature et de cinéma / Talking about literature and cinema
bridge: In French, to express opinions and nuances about books and films, specific structures and tenses are used that do not always have a direct equivalent in Spanish. For example, the French imperfect (imparfait) is often used to describe the context of a story, while the passé composé narrates specific actions. Additionally, the French subjunctive has more restricted uses than in Spanish, especially after opinion expressions like 'je pense que' or 'je crois que', where French uses the indicative. Beware of false friends like 'assister à' (to attend) or 'réaliser' (to realize), which can lead to errors when talking about cinema and literature.
rule: To talk about literature and cinema in French at B2 level, it is key to master: 1) The use of the imparfait for descriptions and the passé composé for specific actions (e.g., 'Le film était intéressant, mais j'ai trouvé la fin décevante'). 2) Expressing opinion with the indicative after verbs like 'penser', 'croire', 'trouver' in affirmative (Je pense que le livre est mieux que le film), but with the subjunctive in negative or interrogative (Je ne pense pas que ce livre soit le meilleur). 3) The subjunctive after expressions of emotion or judgment: 'C'est dommage que...', 'Je suis content(e) que...'. 4) The use of 'devoir' in the conditional for recommendations: 'Tu devrais lire ce roman'. 5) Specific vocabulary: 'un roman', 'une nouvelle', 'un essai', 'un film', 'un réalisateur', 'un acteur', 'une intrigue', 'le dénouement'. 6) To express the development of the plot, the recent past (venir de + infinitif) or the future is used, but with temporal nuances. Pay attention that in French, 'rencontrer' means to meet someone, not to find something, and 'revoir' does not mean to review.

concept_examples.text: Je pense que le roman est plus subtil que le film.
concept_examples.translation: I think the novel is more subtle than the film.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə lə ʁɔmɑ̃ ɛ ply sytil kə lə film/

concept_examples.text: Le réalisateur a réussi à créer une atmosphère unique.
concept_examples.translation: The director managed to create a unique atmosphere.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə ʁealizatœʁ a ʁeysi a kʁee yn atmɔsfɛʁ yn nik/

concept_examples.text: C'est dommage que le film ne soit pas fidèle au livre.
concept_examples.translation: It's a pity that the film is not faithful to the book.
concept_examples.phonetic: /sɛ dɔmaʒ kə lə film nə swa pa fidɛl o livʁ/

concept_examples.text: Tu devrais lire ce roman policier, il est captivant.
concept_examples.translation: You should read this detective novel, it's captivating.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ty dəvʁɛ liʁ sə ʁɔmɑ̃ pɔlisje, il ɛ kaptivɑ̃/

common_error.wrong: Je pense que le film soit meilleur que le livre.
common_error.correct: Je pense que le film est meilleur que le livre.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne pense pas que le film soit meilleur que le livre.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish it is common to use the subjunctive after 'creo que' in affirmative (Creo que sea...), but in French the indicative is used with 'penser que' in affirmative. The error occurs due to direct transfer from Spanish. When the sentence is negative or interrogative, then the subjunctive is used in French: 'Je ne pense pas que...' or 'Penses-tu que...'. Remember: 'penser que' + affirmative -> indicative; 'ne pas penser que' -> subjunctive.

examples.original: À mon avis, le livre est plus riche en détails que le film.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃ avi, lə livʁ ɛ ply ʁiʃ ɑ̃ detaj kə lə film/
examples.translation: In my opinion, the book is richer in details than the film.
examples.note: Use of 'à mon avis' to give an opinion, followed by the indicative. In Spanish we often use 'en mi opinión' or 'a mi parecer'.

examples.original: Je trouve que l'acteur principal est très convaincant.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə laktœʁ pʁɛ̃sipal ɛ tʁɛ kɔ̃vɛ̃kɑ̃/
examples.translation: I find the main actor very convincing.
examples.note: 'Trouver que' + indicative, same as in Spanish 'encontrar que'.

examples.original: Selon moi, la fin du film est prévisible.
examples.phonetic: /səlɑ̃ mwa, la fɛ̃ dy film ɛ pʁevizibl/
examples.translation: In my opinion, the end of the film is predictable.
examples.note: Expression 'selon moi' (in my opinion) is used with the indicative, typical in criticism contexts.

examples.original: Le roman se déroule au XIXe siècle à Paris.
examples.phonetic: /lə ʁɔmɑ̃ sə deʁul o diznɛf sjɛk l a paʁi/
examples.translation: The novel takes place in the 19th century in Paris.
examples.note: Pronominal verb 'se dérouler' (to take place) and use of the preposition 'au' before the century.

examples.original: Le personnage principal est un détective qui mène l'enquête.
examples.phonetic: /lə pɛʁsɔnaʒ pʁɛ̃sipal ɛt‿œ̃ detɛktiv ki mɛn lɑ̃kɛt/
examples.translation: The main character is a detective who leads the investigation.
examples.note: Relative 'qui' functions as subject, same as in Spanish 'que'.

examples.original: L'histoire se termine par une révélation surprenante.
examples.phonetic: /listwaʁ sə tɛʁmin paʁ yn ʁevelasjɔ̃ syʁpʁənɑ̃t/
examples.translation: The story ends with a surprising revelation.
examples.note: Use of 'se terminer par' (to end with), while in Spanish we say 'terminar con' or 'acabar en'.

examples.original: Le film raconte l'histoire d'une jeune femme qui cherche sa vérité.
examples.phonetic: /lə film ʁakɔ̃t listwaʁ dyn ʒœn fam ki ʃɛʁʃ sa veʁite/
examples.translation: The film tells the story of a young woman who seeks her truth.
examples.note: Verb 'raconter' (to tell) and 'une jeune femme' (a young woman). Note the elision of 'une' in 'd'une'.

levels.label: Faire des critiques et des recommandations

examples.original: Ce film vaut le détour, tu ne seras pas déçu(e).
examples.phonetic: /sə film vo lə detuʁ, ty nə səʁa pa desy/
examples.translation: This film is worth the detour, you won't be disappointed.
examples.note: Idiomatic expression 'valoir le détour' (to be worth the detour). The simple future 'tu ne seras pas'.

examples.original: L'auteur aurait pu développer davantage les personnages secondaires.
examples.phonetic: /lotœʁ ɔʁe py devləpe davɑ̃taʒ le pɛʁsɔnaʒ səɡɔ̃dɛʁ/
examples.translation: The author could have developed the secondary characters more.
examples.note: Compound conditional 'aurait pu' to criticize something that was not done.

examples.original: Je vous recommande de lire ce roman avant de voir le film.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vu ʁəkɔmɑ̃d də liʁ sə ʁɔmɑ̃ avɑ̃ də vwaʁ lə film/
examples.translation: I recommend you read this novel before seeing the film.
examples.note: Use of 'recommander de + infinitive', structure with implicit subjunctive.

examples.original: Le scénario n'est pas assez original, mais la mise en scène est brillante.
examples.phonetic: /lə senaʁjo nɛ pa ase ɔʁiʒinal, mɛ la mizɑ̃ sɛn ɛ bʁijɑ̃t/
examples.translation: The screenplay is not original enough, but the staging is brilliant.
examples.note: Expression 'mise en scène' (staging). Adjective 'assez' (enough).

title: Parler de sujets scientifiques et médicaux / Talking about scientific and medical topics
bridge: In French, scientific and medical vocabulary shares many roots with Spanish, but beware of false friends: 'expérience' means 'experiment' and also 'experience', while 'experience' in Spanish translates to 'expérience' in that sense; 'sensible' in French means 'sensible' in the sense of 'easily feeling', not 'sensato' (which is 'sensé'). Additionally, the impersonal pronoun 'on' is used very frequently in scientific contexts (equivalent to 'se' in Spanish), but note that 'on' is conjugated as 'il/elle'. The structure 'il est important de + infinitif' is very common, whereas in Spanish we usually use 'es importante + infinitivo'.
rule: To talk about scientific and medical topics in French at B2 level, you need to handle: 1) The present indicative for general facts (e.g., 'le cœur bat'), 2) The passé composé for results or discoveries (e.g., 'les chercheurs ont découvert'), 3) The simple future for predictions ('on trouvera'), 4) The conditional for hypotheses ('cela pourrait'), 5) The subjunctive after impersonal expressions ('il est essentiel que', 'il faut que'), 6) The use of 'on' instead of 'nous' in formal contexts, 7) Specific vocabulary: names of diseases, parts of the body, verbs like 'soigner', 'guérir', 'prévenir', 'diagnostiquer', 8) Logical connectors: 'par conséquent', 'en revanche', 'c'est pourquoi'. Practice the pronunciation of terms like 'sang' (with the voiced [s]) and 'cerveau' (where 'eau' is pronounced as /o/). Note that the French accent is less marked than Spanish, but liaison is important: 'les hôpitaux' is pronounced /lez‿o.pi.to/.

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel de se laver les mains avant les repas.
concept_examples.translation: It is essential to wash your hands before meals.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛ.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl də sə la.ve le mɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ le ʁə.pa/

concept_examples.text: Les chercheurs ont récemment découvert un nouveau traitement.
concept_examples.translation: Researchers recently discovered a new treatment.
concept_examples.phonetic: /le ʃɛʁ.ʃø.z‿ɔ̃ ʁe.sa.mɑ̃ de.ku.vɛ.ʁ‿œ̃ nu.vo tʁɛt.mɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: On sait que le tabac augmente le risque de cancer du poumon.
concept_examples.translation: It is known that smoking increases the risk of lung cancer.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ sɛ kə lə ta.ba ɔɡ.mɑ̃t lə ʁisk də kɑ̃.sɛʁ dy pu.mɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Si les symptômes persistent, vous devriez consulter un médecin.
concept_examples.translation: If symptoms persist, you should see a doctor.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si le sɛ̃p.tom pɛʁ.sist, vu də.vʁje kɔ̃.syl.te œ̃ med.sɛ̃/

common_error.wrong: Je suis confus sur ce diagnostic.
common_error.correct: Je suis perplexe face à ce diagnostic.
common_error.correct_alt: Je ne comprends pas bien ce diagnostic.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, 'confuso' can mean 'perplexed' or 'bewildered', but in French, 'confus' means 'embarrassed' or 'confused' in the sense of 'unclear'. To express perplexity, 'perplexe' or 'déconcerté' is used. This error is common due to the false friend between 'confuso' and 'confus'.

levels.label: Le corps humain et la santé

examples.original: Le cœur est un muscle qui pompe le sang dans tout le corps.
examples.phonetic: /lə kœʁ ɛ.t‿œ̃ myskl ki pɔ̃p lə sɑ̃ dɑ̃ tu lə kɔʁ/
examples.translation: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood throughout the body.
examples.note: Note that 'cœur' is pronounced /kœʁ/ with the rounded vowel /ø/. 'Sang' ends with a nasal consonant; the 'g' is not pronounced.

examples.original: Le cerveau contrôle toutes nos fonctions vitales.
examples.phonetic: /lə sɛʁ.vo kɔ̃.tʁɔl tut no fɔ̃k.sjɔ̃ vi.tal/
examples.translation: The brain controls all our vital functions.
examples.note: 'Cerveau' may look like a false friend, but it is pronounced /sɛʁ.vo/. The ending '-eau' is pronounced /o/.

examples.original: Elle souffre d'une maladie chronique des reins.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl sufʁ dyn ma.la.di kʁɔ.nik de ʁɛ̃/
examples.translation: She suffers from a chronic kidney disease.
examples.note: The preposition 'de' contracts with the definite article 'les' to form 'des'.

examples.original: Il faut éviter la sédentarité pour rester en bonne santé.
examples.phonetic: /il fo e.vi.te la se.dɑ̃.ta.ʁi.te puʁ ʁɛs.te ɑ̃ bɔn sɑ̃.te/
examples.translation: You must avoid a sedentary lifestyle to stay healthy.
examples.note: The construction 'il faut + infinitif' is very common in French, equivalent to 'hay que' or 'it is necessary'.

examples.original: Les scientifiques analysent les données pour vérifier leurs hypothèses.
examples.phonetic: /le sjɑ̃.ti.fik a.na.liz le dɔ.ne puʁ ve.ʁi.fje lœʁ i.pɔ.tɛz/
examples.translation: Scientists analyze data to verify their hypotheses.
examples.note: The plural of 'hypothèse' is 'hypothèses' and sounds the same in singular and plural; only the article changes. Pay attention to the pronunciation of 'données' (with /ɔ̃/ nasal).

examples.original: L'expérience a montré que le médicament était efficace.
examples.phonetic: /lɛk.spe.ʁjɑ̃s a mɔ̃.tʁe kə lə me.di.ka.mɑ̃ e.tɛ e.fi.kas/
examples.translation: The experiment showed that the medication was effective.
examples.note: Be careful: 'expérience' can mean 'experiment' or 'experience'. In a scientific context, it usually means 'experiment'. 'Médicament' is pronounced /me.di.ka.mɑ̃/.

examples.original: Le développement de nouveaux vaccins nécessite des années de recherche.
examples.phonetic: /lə de.vlɔp.mɑ̃ də nu.vo vak.sɛ̃ ne.se.sit de za.ne də ʁə.ʃɛʁʃ/
examples.translation: The development of new vaccines requires years of research.
examples.note: Observe the liaison between 'des' and 'années' (/de za.ne/). 'Recherche' is used without an article for 'research' in this context.

levels.label: Discuter des traitements et de la prévention

examples.original: Le médecin m'a conseillé de prendre des antibiotiques pendant une semaine.
examples.phonetic: /lə med.sɛ̃ ma kɔ̃.se.je də pʁɑ̃dʁ de zɑ̃.ti.bjɔ.tik pɑ̃.dɑ̃ yn sə.mɛn/
examples.translation: The doctor advised me to take antibiotics for a week.
examples.note: The verb 'conseiller' is constructed with 'de + infinitif' when there is an indirect object. Notice the pronunciation of 'm'a' as /ma/ with elision.

examples.original: Une alimentation équilibrée et une activité physique régulière sont essentielles pour prévenir les maladies cardiovasculaires.
examples.phonetic: /yn al.mɑ̃.ta.sjɔ̃ e.ki.li.bʁe e yn ak.ti.vi.te fi.zik ʁe.ɡy.ljɛʁ sɔ̃.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl puʁ pʁe.vniʁ le ma.la.di kaʁ.djo.vas.ky.lɛʁ/
examples.translation: A balanced diet and regular physical activity are essential to prevent cardiovascular diseases.
examples.note: The agreement of 'essentielles' with the plural subject. Observe the liaison with 'sont' and 'essentielles' (/sɔ̃.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl/).

examples.original: Il est crucial de respecter les doses prescrites par le pharmacien.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ kʁy.sjal də ʁɛs.pɛk.te le doz pʁɛs.kʁit paʁ lə faʁ.ma.sjɛ̃/
examples.translation: It is crucial to follow the doses prescribed by the pharmacist.
examples.note: The construction 'il est crucial de + infinitif' followed by subjunctive in the subordinate clause if used with 'que'. Here, 'par' indicates the agent (by).

examples.original: La vaccination reste le moyen le plus efficace de se protéger contre la grippe.
examples.phonetic: /la vak.si.na.sjɔ̃ ʁɛst lə mwa.jɛ̃ lə plys e.fi.kas də sə pʁɔ.te.ʒe kɔ̃.tʁə la ɡʁip/
examples.translation: Vaccination remains the most effective way to protect oneself against the flu.
examples.note: The superlative 'le plus efficace' is used with 'de' to indicate the complement. 'Se protéger contre' is a fixed expression.

translations.en: Talking about scientific and medical topics

title: Débattre de questions politiques et sociales / Debating political and social issues
bridge: In Spanish, to express opinions on political and social topics we often use the subjunctive after impersonal expressions like 'es importante que' or 'es necesario que'. In French, the subjunctive is used similarly, but you need to be careful with conjunctions like 'bien que' (even though) and 'pour que' (so that) which always require the subjunctive. Additionally, in French, connectors like 'certes... mais' (admittedly... but) structure discourse differently. Pay attention to the use of the conditional for suggestions and the 'ne explétif' in some formal expressions.
rule: To debate at B2 level in French, it is essential to master the following structures: 1) The subjunctive after impersonal opinion expressions: 'il est important que + subjunctive', 'il est essentiel que', 'il faut que'. 2) Conjunctions that govern the subjunctive: 'bien que', 'quoique' (even though), 'pour que' (so that), 'afin que' (so that), 'à moins que' (unless), 'avant que' (before). 3) The conditional for suggestions and politeness: 'je voudrais', 'il faudrait', 'on pourrait'. 4) The 'ne explétif' after expressions of fear or negation: 'je crains qu'il ne vienne' (I fear he might come). 5) Indirect speech to report opinions: 'selon lui...', 'd'après le gouvernement...'. 6) Argumentative connectors: 'en premier lieu' (firstly), 'en outre' (furthermore), 'par conséquent' (consequently), 'néanmoins' (nevertheless). Note that in French the subjunctive is not used after 'après que' (after), unlike what many Spanish speakers assume; the indicative is used instead.

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel que les citoyens participent aux élections.
concept_examples.translation: It is essential that citizens participate in elections.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿esɑ̃sjɛl kə le sitwaɛ̃ paʁtisip o eleksjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Bien que le gouvernement ait promis des réformes, rien n'a changé.
concept_examples.translation: Even though the government has promised reforms, nothing has changed.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə lə ɡuvɛʁnəmɑ̃ ɛ pʁɔmi de ʁefɔʁm, ʁjɛ̃ n‿a ʃɑ̃ʒe/

concept_examples.text: On pourrait envisager une fiscalité plus progressive.
concept_examples.translation: We could consider a more progressive tax system.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ pʁuʁe ɑ̃vizaʒe yn fiskalite ply pʁɔɡʁɛsiv/

concept_examples.text: Je crains que les inégalités n'augmentent encore.
concept_examples.translation: I fear that inequalities may increase even more.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə kʁɛ̃ kə lez‿ineɡalite n‿oɡmɑ̃t ɑ̃kɔʁ/

common_error.wrong: Après que le président a parlé, nous avons discuté. (Using subjunctive: Après que le président ait parlé...)
common_error.correct: Après que le président a parlé, nous avons discuté.
common_error.correct_alt: Après que le président a parlé, nous avons discuté.
common_error.explanation: The most common mistake is using the subjunctive after 'après que' due to the influence of the Spanish 'después de que'. However, in standard French, 'après que' takes the indicative mood. To sound natural, use the indicative after 'après que'. If you want to express anteriority, use 'avant que' + subjunctive (before). Correct example: 'Avant que le président parle, nous discuterons' (Before the president speaks, we will discuss).

examples.original: À mon avis, la réforme des retraites est nécessaire.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔn‿avi, la ʁefɔʁm de ʁɛtʁɛt ɛ neseɛsɛʁ/
examples.translation: In my opinion, the pension reform is necessary.
examples.note: Use 'à mon avis' (in my opinion) and note that in French you do not say 'de mi opinión' as in Spanish.

examples.original: Je suis convaincu que la transition écologique créera des emplois.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi kɔ̃vɛ̃ky kə la tʁɑ̃zisjɔ̃ ekɔlɔʒik kʁea de ɑ̃plwa/
examples.translation: I am convinced that the ecological transition will create jobs.
examples.note: Observe that 'être convaincu que' is followed by the indicative, not the subjunctive.

examples.original: Selon les sondages, la majorité soutient cette mesure.
examples.phonetic: /səlɔ̃ le sɔ̃daʒ, la maʒɔʁite sutjɛ sɛt məzyʁ/
examples.translation: According to the polls, the majority supports this measure.
examples.note: 'Selon' (according to) is formal; in conversation 'd'après' is also used.

examples.original: Certes, le chômage a baissé, mais la précarité augmente.
examples.phonetic: /sɛʁt, lə ʃomaʒ a bɛse, mɛ la pʁekaʁite oɡmɑ̃t/
examples.translation: Admittedly, unemployment has decreased, but precarity is increasing.
examples.note: 'Certes... mais' is a useful connector for nuance, similar to 'ciertamente... pero'.

examples.original: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec vous, car les faits sont différents.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa dakɔʁ avɛk vu, kaʁ le fɛ sɔ̃ difeʁɑ̃/
examples.translation: I do not agree with you, because the facts are different.
examples.note: In formal French, 'car' (because) explains the reason, whereas 'parce que' is more causal.

examples.original: Il est vrai que la situation est complexe, néanmoins il faut agir.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛ vʁɛ kə la sitɥasjɔ̃ ɛ kɔ̃plɛks, neɑ̃mwɛ̃ il fo aʒiʁ/
examples.translation: It is true that the situation is complex, nevertheless action must be taken.
examples.note: 'Néanmoins' (nevertheless) is formal; in conversation 'pourtant' (however) is also used.

examples.original: Si le gouvernement investissait dans l'éducation, les inégalités diminueraient.
examples.phonetic: /si lə ɡuvɛʁnəmɑ̃ ɛ̃vɛstisɛ dɑ̃ l‿edykasjɔ̃, lez‿ineɡalite diminyʁɛ/
examples.translation: If the government invested in education, inequalities would decrease.
examples.note: Use of the conditional for hypotheses: si + imperfect, conditional.

examples.original: Il faudrait renforcer les services publics pour mieux répondre aux besoins.
examples.phonetic: /il fodʁɛ ʁɑ̃fɔʁse le sɛʁvis pyblik puʁ mjø ʁepɔ̃dʁ o bəzwɛ̃/
examples.translation: The public services should be strengthened to better meet needs.
examples.note: 'Il faudrait' (should) is a polite way to suggest.

examples.original: À moins que le climat ne change, les migrations vont s'accentuer.
examples.phonetic: /a mwɛ̃ kə lə klima nə ʃɑ̃ʒ, le miɡʁasjɔ̃ vɔ̃ saksɑ̃tɥe/
examples.translation: Unless the climate changes, migration will intensify.
examples.note: With 'à moins que' the subjunctive is used and often the 'ne explétif'.

title: Économie et finances : en parler avec nuance / Economy and finance: speaking with nuance
bridge: In French, when talking about economy and finance, certain structures differ from Spanish. For example, the use of 'de' after verbs like 'parler de' or 'discuter de' is mandatory, whereas in Spanish, 'hablar de' or 'discutir sobre' can sometimes be used without a preposition. Additionally, French uses 'il faut' + infinitive to express impersonal obligation, similar to 'hay que' in Spanish, but with nuances of formality. Be careful with false friends: 'monnaie' does not mean 'moneda' (in the sense of currency) but rather 'change' or 'currency' in general, and 'bénéfice' does not mean 'beneficio' in the sense of favor, but rather 'profit'.
rule: To discuss finance in French at a B2 level, it is essential to master: 1) Specific vocabulary (le budget, l'épargne, l'investissement, le taux d'intérêt, la bourse, etc.). 2) Expressions of quantity and proportion: 'une hausse de', 'une baisse de', 'un pourcentage de'. 3) Impersonal obligation with 'il faut' + infinitive: 'Il faut épargner pour l'avenir'. 4) The subjunctive mood in sentences like 'Il est important que vous investissiez' (it is important that you invest). 5) The conditional for advice: 'Vous devriez diversifier vos placements' (you should diversify your investments). 6) The difference between 'acheter' (to buy) and 'payer' (to pay): 'J'achète des actions' (I buy stocks) vs. 'Je paie mes impôts' (I pay my taxes). 7) Use of 'depuis' with the present tense for ongoing actions: 'J'épargne depuis cinq ans' (I have been saving for five years).

concept_examples.text: Il faut épargner pour assurer notre retraite.
concept_examples.translation: One must save to secure our retirement.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fo e.paʁ.ɲe puʁ a.sy.ʁe nɔtʁ ʁə.tʁɛt/

concept_examples.text: Le taux d'intérêt a augmenté de 0,5 % cette année.
concept_examples.translation: The interest rate has increased by 0.5% this year.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə to dɛ̃.te.ʁɛ a oɡ.mɑ̃.te də siŋk puʁ.sɑ̃ sɛt a.ne/

concept_examples.text: Nous devrions diversifier nos placements pour réduire les risques.
concept_examples.translation: We should diversify our investments to reduce risks.
concept_examples.phonetic: /nu də.vʁjɔ̃ di.vɛʁ.si.fje no plas.mɑ̃ puʁ ʁe.dɥiʁ le ʁisk/

concept_examples.text: Il est important que vous investissiez dans des projets durables.
concept_examples.translation: It is important that you invest in sustainable projects.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃ kə vu ɛ̃.vɛs.ti.sje dɑ̃ de pʁɔ.ʒɛ dy.ʁabl/

common_error.wrong: J'ai besoin d'acheter des actions, mais je ne comprends pas les risques.
common_error.correct: J'ai besoin d'acheter des actions, mais je ne comprends pas les risques.
common_error.explanation: This example is correct. To illustrate a common error, let's use: 'Je veux investir sur la bourse' (a direct translation from Spanish 'invertir en la bolsa'). In French, it is 'investir en Bourse' or 'investir dans la Bourse'. Another frequent mistake: 'discuter sur' instead of 'discuter de'. For example: 'Nous avons discuté sur le budget' (incorrect) -> 'Nous avons discuté du budget' (correct). Also: 'payer pour' when 'payer' should be used without a preposition: 'J'ai payé pour le café' (incorrect if referring to paying for the coffee, it should be 'J'ai payé le café').

examples.original: Le budget mensuel est de 2 000 euros.
examples.phonetic: /lə byd.ʒe mɑ̃.sɥɛl ɛ də dø mil ø.ʁo/
examples.translation: The monthly budget is 2000 euros.
examples.note: Note: 'budget' is masculine in French, just like in Spanish. The preposition 'de' is used to indicate quantity.

examples.original: L'épargne est importante pour les imprévus.
examples.phonetic: /le.paʁɲ ɛ.t‿ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃t puʁ le.z‿ɛ̃.pʁe.vy/
examples.translation: Savings are important for unexpected expenses.
examples.note: 'L'épargne' (feminine) is used in the singular, unlike Spanish which may use 'ahorros' in the plural.

examples.original: Les impôts augmentent chaque année.
examples.phonetic: /le.z‿ɛ̃.po oɡ.mɑ̃t ʃak a.ne/
examples.translation: Taxes increase every year.
examples.note: 'Impôts' is plural and takes 'les'. Be careful with the pronunciation of the final 's' in 'impôts', which is not pronounced.

examples.original: Elle a investi dans une start-up.
examples.phonetic: /ɛl a ɛ̃.vɛs.ti dɑ̃ yn staʁ.tœp/
examples.translation: She invested in a startup.
examples.note: It is 'investir dans' (not 'sur'), just like in Spanish 'invertir en'. 'Start-up' is a common anglicism.

examples.original: Le chômage a baissé de 2 % au dernier trimestre.
examples.phonetic: /lə ʃo.maʒ a bɛ.se də dø puʁ.sɑ̃ o dɛʁ.nje tʁi.mɛstʁ/
examples.translation: Unemployment has decreased by 2% in the last quarter.
examples.note: Use of 'baisser de' to indicate the amount of the decrease. In Spanish, we say 'bajar un 2%', but in French 'de' is used.

examples.original: La bourse est en hausse depuis quelques semaines.
examples.phonetic: /la buʁs ɛ.t‿ɑ̃ os də.pɥi kɛlk sə.mɛn/
examples.translation: The stock market has been rising for a few weeks.
examples.note: 'En hausse' is a fixed expression. 'Depuis' with the present tense indicates that the action is ongoing.

examples.original: Les prix ont grimpé de manière significative.
examples.phonetic: /le pʁi ɔ̃ ɡʁɛ̃.pe də ma.njɛʁ si.ɲi.fi.ka.tiv/
examples.translation: Prices have climbed significantly.
examples.note: Use of 'grimper' (to climb) in informal contexts. 'De manière' is equivalent to 'de manera' in Spanish, but 'de façon' is preferred in more formal registers.

examples.original: On observe une chute de la demande.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ ɔp.sɛʁv yn ʃyt də la də.mɑ̃d/
examples.translation: A drop in demand is observed.
examples.note: 'Chute' is feminine. 'On' is used instead of 'nous' in spoken French and often as an impersonal subject.

levels.label: Exprimer des opinions et des conseils

examples.original: À mon avis, l'État devrait investir dans les énergies renouvelables.
examples.phonetic: /a mɔ̃.n‿a.vi le.ta də.vʁɛ ɛ̃.vɛs.tiʁ dɑ̃ le.z‿e.nɛʁ.ʒi ʁə.nu.və.labl/
examples.translation: In my opinion, the government should invest in renewable energies.
examples.note: Use of the conditional 'devrait' to give advice. 'À mon avis' is similar to 'in my opinion'.

examples.original: Je pense qu'il est essentiel de réduire nos dépenses inutiles.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pɑ̃s kil ɛ.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl də ʁe.dɥiʁ no de.pɑ̃s i.ny.til/
examples.translation: I think it is essential to reduce our unnecessary expenses.
examples.note: 'Il est essentiel de' + infinitive. Note that 'de' is used before the infinitive.

examples.original: Si j'étais vous, j'investirais dans l'immobilier locatif.
examples.phonetic: /si ʒe.tɛ vu ʒ‿ɛ̃.vɛs.ti.ʁɛ dɑ̃ l‿i.mɔ.bi.lje lɔ.ka.tif/
examples.translation: If I were you, I would invest in rental property.
examples.note: Conditional structure with 'si + imparfait, conditionnel'. French uses 'si j'étais vous', just like in Spanish.

examples.original: Il vaut mieux épargner maintenant plutôt que d'emprunter plus tard.
examples.phonetic: /il vo mjø e.paʁ.ɲe mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃ ply.to kə dɑ̃.pʁœ̃.te ply taʁ/
examples.translation: It is better to save now than to borrow more later.
examples.note: 'Il vaut mieux' + infinitive. 'Plutôt que de' + infinitive to compare actions.

title: Exprimer des idées abstraites / Expressing abstract ideas
bridge: In Spanish, we use the subjunctive to express hypotheses or conditions (e.g., 'si yo fuera', 'si tuviera'). In French, the use of the imperfect subjunctive is much more restricted and formal; in everyday conversation, it is replaced by the indicative or conditional. Additionally, French uses the subjunctive after impersonal expressions like 'il faut que' or 'il est important que', whereas in Spanish we sometimes use the indicative with 'es importante que' + subjunctive (similar, but be careful with tenses). Another common mistake: 'si + imperfect' in French translates to Spanish as 'si + imperfect', but French does not use the conditional in the 'si' clause, just like in Spanish (correct: 'si j'avais, je ferais'; incorrect: 'si j'aurais').
rule:
To express hypotheses, conditions, and desires in French at a B2 level, you must master:
1) The structure 'si + imparfait, conditionnel présent' for unreal or unlikely hypotheses in the present: 'Si j'avais le temps, j'étudierais la philosophie' (If I had time, I would study philosophy).
2) The present subjunctive after impersonal expressions such as 'il faut que', 'il est important que', 'il est possible que': 'Il faut que je réfléchisse à cette idée' (I must think about this idea).
3) The use of 'pour que' + subjunctive to express purpose: 'Je te l'explique pour que tu comprennes' (I explain this to you so that you understand). Do not use the subjunctive after 'si' or after 'après que' (in modern French, the indicative is used after 'après que').
4) The past conditional for unfulfilled hypotheses: 'J'aurais aimé comprendre cette théorie' (I would have liked to understand that theory).
Remember that in French, the imperfect subjunctive ('que je fisse') is literary and not used in conversation; instead, the present subjunctive or a reformulation is used.

concept_examples.text: Si j'avais le choix, je défendrais cette idée.
concept_examples.translation: If I had the choice, I would defend this idea.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ʒ‿avɛ lə ʃwa, ʒə defɑ̃dʁɛ set‿ide/

concept_examples.text: Il faut que nous réfléchissions à ce concept.
concept_examples.translation: It is necessary that we reflect on this concept.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fo kə nu ʁefleʃisjɔ̃ a sə kɔ̃sɛp/

concept_examples.text: Je te donne cet exemple pour que tu comprennes mieux.
concept_examples.translation: I give you this example so that you understand better.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə tə dɔn sɛt‿ɛgzɑ̃pl puʁ kə ty kɔ̃pʁɛn mjø/

concept_examples.text: J'aurais aimé que tu développes ta réflexion.
concept_examples.translation: I would have liked you to develop your reflection.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒ‿ɔʁɛz‿eme kə ty devlɔp ta ʁeflɛksjɔ̃/

common_error.wrong: Si j'aurais le temps, je ferais plus de philosophie.
common_error.correct: Si j'avais le temps, je ferais plus de philosophie.
common_error.correct_alt: Si j'avais le temps, je ferais plus de philosophie.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, it is common to use 'si tuviera' (imperfect subjunctive), but some Spanish speakers, influenced by the conditional in the main clause, might use 'si + conditional' in French ('si j'aurais'). In French, just like in Spanish, the 'si' clause never takes the conditional. You must use the imperfect indicative ('j'avais') in the condition. To avoid this mistake, remember that 'si' = 'if' and that the structure requires imparfait + conditionnel.

examples.original: Si on considère cette théorie, tout change.
examples.phonetic: /si ɔ̃ kɔ̃sidɛʁ sɛt teɔʁi, tu ʃɑ̃ʒ/
examples.translation: If we consider this theory, everything changes.
examples.note: Use of the present indicative after 'si' for a real or possible condition.

examples.original: Je serais curieux de connaître ton opinion.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə səʁɛ kyʁjø də kɔnɛtʁ tɔ̃ ɔpinjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I would be curious to know your opinion.
examples.note: The conditional expresses politeness or a hypothesis; it is not preceded by 'si'.

examples.original: Si tout le monde pensait comme toi, le monde serait différent.
examples.phonetic: /si tu lə mɔ̃d pɑ̃sɛ kɔm twa, lə mɔ̃d səʁɛ difeʁɑ̃/
examples.translation: If everyone thought like you, the world would be different.
examples.note: Structure: si + imparfait, conditionnel présent.

examples.original: Il est important que l'on réfléchisse aux conséquences.
examples.phonetic: /il‿ɛt‿ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃ kə lɔ̃ ʁefleʃis o kɔ̃sekɑ̃s/
examples.translation: It is important that we reflect on the consequences.
examples.note: Use of the present subjunctive ('réfléchisse') after 'il est important que'.

examples.original: Je préférerais que tu argumentes mieux.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pʁefeʁɛ kə ty aʁɡymɑ̃t mjø/
examples.translation: I would prefer that you argue better.
examples.note: With 'préférer' + que, the subjunctive is used; in Spanish, the subjunctive is also used (argumentes).

examples.original: Pour que cette idée soit claire, il faut la reformuler.
examples.phonetic: /puʁ kə sɛt‿ide swa klɛʁ, il fo la ʁəfɔʁmyle/
examples.translation: So that this idea is clear, it must be reformulated.
examples.note: Purpose is expressed with 'pour que' + subjunctive.

examples.original: Si j'avais su, j'aurais abordé le sujet autrement.
examples.phonetic: /si ʒ‿avɛ sy, ʒ‿ɔʁɛz‿abɔʁde lə syʒɛ otʁəmɑ̃/
examples.translation: If I had known, I would have approached the topic differently.
examples.note: Si + plus-que-parfait, conditionnel passé for past hypotheses.

examples.original: J'aurais aimé que tu sois là pour en débattre.
examples.phonetic: /ʒ‿ɔʁɛz‿eme kə ty swa la puʁ ɑ̃ debatʁ/
examples.translation: I would have liked you to be there to debate it.
examples.note: Past conditional + subjunctive to express an unfulfilled wish.

examples.original: Il aurait fallu que je précise ma pensée.
examples.phonetic: /il‿ɔʁɛ faly kə ʒə pʁesis ma pɑ̃se/
examples.translation: It would have been necessary for me to clarify my thought.
examples.note: Impersonal structure 'il aurait fallu que' + subjunctive.

title: Le subjonctif dans les conversations sur l'art / The subjunctive in conversations about art
bridge: In Spanish, we use the subjunctive after expressions of opinion or emotion (es importante que, me alegro de que). In French, this usage is similar, but there are key differences: in French, the subjunctive is used with verbs like 'penser' only in negative or interrogative forms, and not after 'espérer'. Additionally, the conjugation of the present subjunctive in French has regular endings (-e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent) that are often confused with the indicative because they sound the same. Be careful with irregular verbs like 'être' and 'avoir'.
rule: The French subjunctive is used in subordinate clauses introduced by 'que' when the main clause expresses necessity (il faut que), desire (je veux que), emotion (je suis content que), negative opinion (je ne pense pas que), or doubt (je doute que). It is not used after 'espérer' (to hope) nor in affirmative statements with 'penser' or 'croire' (I think that... uses the indicative). Formation: for regular verbs ending in '-er', '-ir', '-re', take the third person plural of the present indicative (ils parlent) and replace '-ent' with the endings: -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent. Common exceptions: être (sois, sois, soit, soyons, soyez, soient) and avoir (aie, aies, ait, ayons, ayez, aient). Also verbs like 'aller' (aille, ailles, aille, allions, alliez, aillent) and 'faire' (fasse). In conversation, it is often used to give opinions about art: 'Je trouve que ce tableau soit...' (incorrect, because 'trouver' in affirmative takes the indicative).

concept_examples.text: Il est essentiel que l'art reflète la société.
concept_examples.translation: It is essential that art reflects society.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿esɑ̃sjɛl kə laʁt ʁəflɛt la sɔsjete/

concept_examples.text: Je ne pense pas que cette exposition soit intéressante.
concept_examples.translation: I don’t think this exhibition is interesting.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sɛt ɛkspozisjɔ̃ swa ɛ̃teʁɛsɑ̃t/

concept_examples.text: Bien que la peinture soit abstraite, elle évoque des émotions.
concept_examples.translation: Although the painting is abstract, it evokes emotions.
concept_examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə la pɛ̃tyʁ swa apstʁɛt ɛl evɔk de emosjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Il faut que les artistes soient libres de créer.
concept_examples.translation: It is necessary for artists to be free to create.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fo kə le zaʁtist swa libʁ də kʁee/

common_error.wrong: J'espère que la pièce de théâtre soit réussie.
common_error.correct: J'espère que la pièce de théâtre sera réussie.
common_error.correct_alt: J'espère que la pièce de théâtre est réussie.
common_error.explanation: In Spanish, 'espero que' requires the subjunctive ('espero que sea'), but in French, 'espérer' expresses hope and is constructed with the indicative (future or present) because it indicates a probable fact. This Spanish calque leads to incorrect use of the subjunctive. To avoid the error, remember that 'espérer' does not govern the subjunctive, unlike 'souhaiter' (to wish), which does.

levels.label: Exprimer une opinion sur une œuvre
levels.translation: Expressing an opinion about a work

examples.original: Je trouve que ce roman est captivant.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə tʁuv kə sə ʁɔmɑ̃ ɛ kaptivɑ̃/
examples.translation: I find that this novel is captivating.
examples.note: With 'trouver' in the affirmative, the indicative is used, not the subjunctive. This is a common error due to Spanish influence.

examples.original: Je ne crois pas que ce film soit un chef-d'œuvre.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə kʁwa pa kə sə film swa ɛ̃ ʃɛfdœvʁ/
examples.translation: I don’t think this film is a masterpiece.
examples.note: In negation, 'croire' requires the subjunctive. Note the difference with the affirmative: 'Je crois que ce film est...'

examples.original: Il est évident que l'art contemporain est provocateur.
examples.phonetic: /il ɛt‿evidɑ̃ kə laʁt kɔ̃tɑ̃pɔʁɛ̃ ɛ pʁɔvɔkatœʁ/
examples.translation: It is evident that contemporary art is provocative.
examples.note: Expressions of certainty like 'il est évident' use the indicative, unlike 'il est possible' which uses the subjunctive.

levels.label: Exprimer des sentiments et des souhaits

examples.original: Je suis ravi qu'il y ait une rétrospective sur Monet.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi ʁavi k‿il i ɛt yn ʁetʁɔspɛktiv syʁ mɔnɛ/
examples.translation: I’m delighted that there is a retrospective on Monet.
examples.note: The emotion (ravi) triggers the subjunctive. Note the formation: 'ait' is the subjunctive of 'avoir'.

examples.original: Je souhaite que nous visitions le Louvre ensemble.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə swɛt kə nu vizisjɔ̃ lə luvʁ ɑ̃sɑ̃bl/
examples.translation: I wish that we visit the Louvre together.
examples.note: 'Souhaiter' governs the subjunctive. The first-person plural subjunctive ends in '-ions' (visitions).

examples.original: Je préfère que tu choisisses une pièce de théâtre classique.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə pʁefɛʁ kə ty ʃwazis yn pjɛs də teatʁ klasik/
examples.translation: I prefer that you choose a classical play.
examples.note: Verbs ending in -ir have subjunctive forms in '-isse' for tu/il/elle. Compare with the present indicative 'tu choisis'.

levels.label: Parler de l'art et de la culture: nuances et exceptions
levels.translation: Talking about art and culture: nuances and exceptions

examples.original: Bien que le musée soit fermé, on peut voir les œuvres en ligne.
examples.phonetic: /bjɛ̃ kə lə myze swa fɛʁme, ɔ̃ pø vwa le zœvʁ ɑ̃ lɔ̃ɲ/
examples.translation: Although the museum is closed, you can see the works online.
examples.note: 'Bien que' always takes the subjunctive. Note the use of the impersonal pronoun 'on'.

examples.original: C'est le meilleur livre que j'aie lu.
examples.phonetic: /sɛ lə mɛjœʁ livʁ kə ʒ‿ɛ ly/
examples.translation: It’s the best book I’ve ever read.
examples.note: In superlatives and relative clauses with a negative antecedent, we use the subjunctive. 'aie' is the subjunctive of 'avoir', don’t confuse it with the imperative 'aie'.

examples.original: Je doute que cette sculpture soit une authentique antiquité.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə dut kə sɛt skyltyʁ swa yn otɑ̃tik ɑ̃tikite/
examples.translation: I doubt that this sculpture is an authentic antiquity.
examples.note: Doubt ('douter') in the affirmative requires the subjunctive. In contrast, 'ne pas douter' (not to doubt) takes the indicative: 'Je ne doute pas qu'elle est authentique.'

translations.en: The subjunctive in conversations about art

title: Discutir soluciones / Discussing solutions
bridge: In Spanish, to propose solutions we use the subjunctive after 'es necesario que' or the conditional 'deberíamos'. In French, the subjunctive is used similarly ('il faut que' + subjunctive), but there is an important twist: 'il faut' without 'que' is constructed with the infinitive ('il faut trouver'), which has no direct equivalent in Spanish. Additionally, the French conditional ('on pourrait') is more common than the subjunctive in contexts of soft suggestions, and 'si on...' is used for direct proposals, similar to Spanish 'si...' but with or without inversion.
rule: To discuss solutions in French at B2 level, use: 1) 'il faut que' + subjunctive (for impersonal obligation: 'il faut qu'on trouve une solution'), 2) 'il faudrait que' + subjunctive (conditional, more polite), 3) 'on pourrait' + infinitive (suggestion: 'on pourrait essayer'), 4) 'si on' + imperfect (hypothetical proposal: 'si on changeait d'approche'), 5) 'pourquoi pas' + infinitive (alternative: 'pourquoi pas contacter le service'). Remember that the French subjunctive is formed with 'que' + special conjugation (je trouve, tu trouves, il trouve, nous trouvions, vous trouviez, ils trouvent). Common errors: using 'il faut que' + infinitive (incorrect: 'il faut que trouver' - correct: 'il faut trouver'), confusing 'pourrait' with 'pourrait être', and forgetting the subjunctive in 'il est important que'.

concept_examples.text: Il faut qu'on trouve une solution rapidement.
concept_examples.translation: It is necessary that we find a solution quickly.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fo kɔ̃ tʁuv yn sɔlysjɔ̃ ʁapidmɑ̃/

concept_examples.text: On pourrait envisager une autre option.
concept_examples.translation: We could consider another option.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɑ̃vizaʒe yn otʁ ɔpsjɔ̃/

concept_examples.text: Si on changeait de stratégie, cela résoudrait peut-être le problème.
concept_examples.translation: If we changed our strategy, that might solve the problem.
concept_examples.phonetic: /si ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒɛ də stʁateʒi səla ʁezudʁɛ pøtɛtʁ lə pʁɔblɛm/

concept_examples.text: Il faudrait que tout le monde participe à la discussion.
concept_examples.translation: It would be necessary for everyone to participate in the discussion.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fodʁɛ kə tu lə mɔ̃d paʁtisip a la diskysjɔ̃/

common_error.wrong: Il faut que nous trouver une solution.
common_error.correct: Il faut que nous trouvions une solution.
common_error.correct_alt: Il nous faut trouver une solution.
common_error.explanation: The error is using the infinitive 'trouver' instead of the subjunctive 'trouvions' after 'que'. In Spanish, the structure 'es necesario que + subjunctive' is parallel, but the student may transfer the Spanish infinitive construction ('es necesario encontrar') to French. Remember: 'il faut que' always requires the subjunctive (or infinitive without 'que': 'il faut trouver'), and for the subjunctive of 'trouver' with 'nous', use 'trouvions' (with -ions). The alternative 'il nous faut trouver' is an equivalent option without subjunctive, but more formal.

examples.original: On pourrait essayer de contacter le client demain.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ puʁɛ ɛsɛje də kɔ̃takte lə kljɑ̃ dəmɛ̃/
examples.translation: We could try contacting the client tomorrow.
examples.note: Conditional 'pourrait' + infinitive for a soft suggestion. Equivalent to Spanish 'podríamos'.

examples.original: Pourquoi pas proposer une réunion en ligne ?
examples.phonetic: /puʁkwa pa pʁopoze yn ʁeyɲɔ̃ ɑ̃ lɔɲ/
examples.translation: Why not propose an online meeting?
examples.note: 'Pourquoi pas' + infinitive for an informal alternative. Spanish '¿por qué no?' also works, but the infinitive is common in French.

examples.original: Si on choisissait une autre date, ce serait plus facile.
examples.phonetic: /si ɔ̃ ʃwazisɛ yn otʁ dat sə sɛʁe ply fasil/
examples.translation: If we chose another date, it would be easier.
examples.note: Hypothetical with 'si' + imperfect in the condition, conditional in the result. Same as in Spanish.

examples.original: La meilleure solution serait de réduire les coûts.
examples.phonetic: /la mɛjœʁ sɔlysjɔ̃ səʁɛ də ʁedyiʁ le ku/
examples.translation: The best solution would be to reduce costs.
examples.note: Use of conditional 'serait' to express a hypothetical evaluation. Similar to Spanish 'sería'.

examples.original: Il vaut mieux attendre avant de prendre une décision.
examples.phonetic: /il vo mjø atɑ̃dʁ avɑ̃ də pʁɑ̃dʁ yn desizjɔ̃/
examples.translation: It is better to wait before making a decision.
examples.note: 'Il vaut mieux' + infinitive expresses preference. Used instead of 'es mejor que' + subjunctive in Spanish.

examples.original: Cette option ne me semble pas très viable.
examples.phonetic: /sɛt ɔpsjɔ̃ nə mə sɑ̃bl pa tʁɛ vjabl/
examples.translation: This option doesn't seem very viable to me.
examples.note: Verb 'sembler' with negation to evaluate. Structure similar to Spanish 'me parece', but remember the French double negative 'ne...pas'.

examples.original: On devrait prendre en compte les risques avant de se décider.
examples.phonetic: /ɔ̃ dəvʁɛ pʁɑ̃dʁ ɑ̃ kɔ̃t le ʁisk avɑ̃ də sə deside/
examples.translation: We should take the risks into account before deciding.
examples.note: Conditional 'devrait' for strong advice. In Spanish we use 'deberíamos', but in French it does not take the subjunctive.

levels.label: Exprimer un accord ou un désaccord (Expresar acuerdo o desacuerdo)

examples.original: Je suis tout à fait d'accord avec cette proposition.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi tut‿a fɛ dakɔʁ avɛk sɛt pʁopozisjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I completely agree with this proposal.
examples.note: Expression of full agreement. Remember the elision: 'd'accord' and the liaison in 'tout à fait'.

examples.original: Je ne suis pas sûr que ce soit la meilleure option.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə nə sɥi pa syʁ kə sə swa la mɛjœʁ ɔpsjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I'm not sure that this is the best option.
examples.note: Subjunctive 'soit' after 'que' following an expression of doubt. This is difficult for Spanish speakers because 'es' becomes 'soit'.

examples.original: Je suis contre cette idée, car elle ne résout pas le problème.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə sɥi kɔ̃tʁ sɛt ide kaʁ ɛl nə ʁezu pa lə pʁɔblɛm/
examples.translation: I am against this idea because it doesn't solve the problem.
examples.note: To express disagreement, use 'être contre' (to be against). In Spanish 'estoy en contra', in French the preposition 'contre' does not take 'de'.

examples.original: D'un côté je comprends, mais de l'autre, ça me semble risqué.
examples.phonetic: /dɛ̃ kote ʒə kɔ̃pʁɑ̃ mɛ də lotʁ sa mə sɑ̃bl ʁiske/
examples.translation: On the one hand I understand, but on the other, it seems risky to me.
examples.note: Concessive structure 'd'un côté... mais de l'autre'. Introduces nuances, very useful in B2 discussions.

title: Exprimer ses objectifs et son développement personnel / Express goals and personal growth
bridge: In French, the subjunctive is often used after expressions of desire and necessity when talking about goals and personal development, similar to Spanish but with differences in tense agreement. Another key difference is the use of 'y' instead of 'e' before vowels (e.g., 'et' does not change). Additionally, French uses 'on' as an informal equivalent of 'we,' which can confuse Spanish speakers. There are also false friends like 'réaliser' (to realize/become aware) vs. 'realizar' (to achieve).
rule: To express goals and personal development in French, structures such as: 1) 'avoir pour objectif de' + infinitive, 2) 'viser à' + infinitive, 3) 'chercher à' + infinitive are used. The subjunctive is required after 'il faut que' or 'je veux que' (e.g., 'il faut que je progresse'). The simple future is used for long-term goals (e.g., 'je deviendrai'). Connectors like 'afin de' (in order to) and 'grâce à' (thanks to) are also common. The conditional expresses hypothetical wishes (e.g., 'je voudrais'). Common errors include using 'réaliser' for 'lograr' (should be 'atteindre' or 'accomplir') or confusing 'but' (goal) with 'bout' (end).

concept_examples.text: J'aimerais atteindre mes objectifs professionnels cette année.
concept_examples.translation: I would like to achieve my professional goals this year.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒɛmʁɛ atɛ̃dʁ me ɔbʒɛktif pʁɔfɛsjɔnɛl sɛt ane/

concept_examples.text: Il faut que je me concentre sur mon développement personnel.
concept_examples.translation: I need to focus on my personal development.
concept_examples.phonetic: /il fo kə ʒə mə kɔ̃sɑ̃tʁ syʁ mɔ̃ devlɔpmɑ̃ pɛʁsɔnɛl/

concept_examples.text: Je vise à améliorer ma confiance en moi.
concept_examples.translation: I aim to improve my self-confidence.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʒə viz a ameljɔʁe ma kɔ̃fjɑ̃s ɑ̃ mwa/

concept_examples.text: Grâce à la persévérance, je réaliserai mes rêves.
concept_examples.translation: Thanks to perseverance, I will make my dreams come true.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɡʁas a la pɛʁseveʁɑ̃s, ʒə ʁealizəʁe me ʁɛv/

common_error.explanation: The French verb 'réaliser' means 'to realize' or 'to become aware of' in specific contexts, but for 'to achieve' goals, 'atteindre' or 'accomplir' should be used. Due to the influence of Spanish 'realizar,' Spanish speakers often misuse 'réaliser.' To avoid this, remember that 'réaliser' is used for dreams or films, while 'atteindre' or 'accomplir' is used for concrete goals.

examples.original: Je souhaite améliorer mon équilibre travail-vie.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə swɛt ameljɔʁe mɔ̃n‿ekilibʁ tʁavaj vi/
examples.translation: I wish to improve my work-life balance.
examples.note: The verb 'souhaiter' followed by an infinitive is common for expressing wishes. Note that 'souhaiter' does not take 'de' before the infinitive.

examples.original: Mon but est de devenir plus autonome.
examples.phonetic: /mɔ̃ byt e də dəvniʁ plys otɔnɔm/
examples.translation: My goal is to become more self-reliant.
examples.note: 'But' means 'goal,' and the structure 'mon but est de + infinitive' is frequently used.

examples.original: J'ai l'intention de me former davantage.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ lɛ̃tɑ̃sjɔ̃ də mə fɔʁme davɑ̃taʒ/
examples.translation: I intend to train further.
examples.note: The expression 'avoir l'intention de' is equivalent to 'tener la intención de' in Spanish.

levels.label: Parler des obstacles et des progrès

examples.original: Je surmonte les obstacles grâce à ma détermination.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə syʁmɔ̃t le ɔpstakl ɡʁas a ma detɛʁminasjɔ̃/
examples.translation: I overcome obstacles thanks to my determination.
examples.note: The verb 'surmonter' specifically means 'to overcome' obstacles; 'passer' is not used in this context.

examples.original: J'ai fait des progrès significatifs dans ma carrière.
examples.phonetic: /ʒɛ fɛ de pʁɔɡʁɛ siɲifikatif dɑ̃ ma kaʁjɛʁ/
examples.translation: I have made significant progress in my career.
examples.note: The phrase 'faire des progrès' is used like the Spanish 'hacer progresos,' but without the definite article.

examples.original: Chaque échec est une opportunité d'apprendre.
examples.phonetic: /ʃak eʃɛk e t‿yn ɔpɔʁtynite d‿apʁɑ̃dʁ/
examples.translation: Every failure is an opportunity to learn.
examples.note: The elision in 'd'apprendre' is mandatory. Note that 'échec' is masculine.

levels.label: Exprimer des projets à long terme

examples.original: D'ici dix ans, je serai devenu un expert dans mon domaine.
examples.phonetic: /disi diz‿ɑ̃, ʒə səʁe dəvny œ̃n‿ɛkspɛʁ dɑ̃ mɔ̃ dɔmɛn/
examples.translation: Within ten years, I will have become an expert in my field.
examples.note: The future perfect tense is used for completed future achievements. 'D'ici' means 'within' in this context.

examples.original: Afin de progresser, je devrai sortir de ma zone de confort.
examples.phonetic: /afɛ̃ də pʁɔɡʁese, ʒə dəvʁe sɔʁtiʁ də ma zɔn də kɔ̃fɔʁ/
examples.translation: To progress, I will have to step out of my comfort zone.
examples.note: 'Afin de' (in order to) is formal and used with the infinitive. This is an example of formal register.

examples.original: Je voudrais créer mon entreprise d'ici quelques années.
examples.phonetic: /ʒə vudʁɛ kʁee mɔ̃n‿ɑ̃tʁəpʁiz disi kɛlkəz‿ane/
examples.translation: I would like to start my own business in a few years.
examples.note: The conditional 'voudrais' expresses polite desire, commonly used in conversation.

examples.original: Il faudra que je m'investisse davantage dans ce projet.
examples.phonetic: /il fodʁa kə ʒə mɛ̃vɛstis davɑ̃taʒ dɑ̃ sə pʁɔʒɛ/
examples.translation: I will need to get more involved in this project.
examples.note: The subjunctive 'm'investisse' after 'faudra que' is mandatory. Observe the future tense agreement in the main clause and subjunctive in the subordinate clause.
